title: Data-center moratoria: who gets paid for permission to build
map_limitation: Four blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) The two links that set every other link's schedule publish nothing an investor can buy or an EDGAR search can read. organized-opposition and state-moratoria-and-siting-law are county boards, petition drives, a governor's office and state commissions, so both carry zero tickers by design and every number on them is a third-party count (Futura-Sciences and programs.com restating Data Center Watch, MultiState and ArentFox Schiff on bill volume), never an issuer disclosure. Data Center Watch's own Q1 2026 page carries no publication date on the fetched version, so its figures are cited here only through two dated pages that quote them. (2) Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search is close to useless on this chain, because the work is bought as professional services rather than as a component. ERM, Ramboll, GHD, SLR, Golder, Burns & McDonnell, Black & Veatch, Sargent & Lundy, 1898 & Co, Guidehouse, Concentric Energy Advisors and every land-use firm that drafts a community benefit agreement are private, and most listed names that do this work file outside the SEC: STN.TO, WSP.TO, ARCAD.AS, AFRY.ST, SWEC-B.ST, VIE.PA, 6370.T, 6368.T, WPP.L, GMG.AX, NXT.AX, AJBU.SI, SGRO.L, MRL.MC, YTLPOWR.KL, ENR.DE, SU.PA, HPS-A.TO, 9432.T, 9984.T and 0700.HK. Those reach the map through research, not through fts. (3) Non-US ticker share is 24 of 64 and that is a property of the occurrence, not an omission. organized-opposition, state-moratoria-and-siting-law, utility-ratemaking-and-large-load-tariffs and us-secondary-market-shift are US state law and US regulated utilities; putting a foreign name on any of them would be invention. The global half of this chain lives at permitting-and-environmental-consultancy, entitled-powered-land and offshore-and-periphery-capacity. (4) The softest claim on the map is the edge from state-moratoria-and-siting-law to offshore-and-periphery-capacity. Nothing fetched this run says a US state freeze sent a named project abroad. What is cited is the mechanism operating: JLL's EMEA mid-year report moving hyper scale sites from 46 km to 175 km from hub cities, greenfield from 8% to 39% of the 2026 to 2028 pipeline, and Ireland's framework redirecting capital rather than releasing it. A screen built on that link must treat it as directional. Two further quantities are soft: no fetched source isolates a data-center permitting margin at any consultancy, and no fetched source prices the premium on an entitled site, so capture at links 4 and 7 cannot be read off the market-size numbers that are cited.

notes.text: SHARED-STAGE DECLARATION, campaign blocker BLK-04. This chain carries power-equipment-shared at position 8 and it IS ai-infrastructure/power-equipment: same stage, same seven tickers, deliberately identical so the duplication is visible on the map instead of discovered in a census. No issuer on that link may be counted toward this theme's issuer coverage; they belong to ai-infrastructure/power-equipment. It is included rather than omitted because utility-ratemaking-and-large-load-tariffs exists precisely to decide who funds the grid upgrade, and a map that says somebody pays without naming what is bought is incomplete. The rank-8 theme minor-nsr-permits (SIG-20260830-05) touches the same layer from the on-site generation side and owes the same declaration when it is built.

THE THESIS WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED, and it survives with one correction and one live risk. Tested: does a freeze relocate rather than delete committed capex? Cited both ways. For relocation: GE Vernova booked over $5 billion of data center orders year-to-date with total orders +88% organically through the same window the moratorium wave accelerated, and JLL puts nearly 100 GW of additions between 2026 and 2030. Against it: Build Inc cites a Sightline Climate estimate that 30 to 50 percent of the 2026 pipeline may be delayed or not delivered, which is deletion, not relocation, and it is on the map at hyperscale-buildout-demand rather than argued away. THE CORRECTION: the signal treats permitting consultancy as a beneficiary. It is, in volume; it is also ARCH-002 in a consultancy costume, mandatory work that is competitively bid, so its capture ceiling is recorded in capture_inputs before the heat run can read scarcity into a $25bn market number.

ARCHETYPES APPLIED. ARCH-002 twice: permitting-and-environmental-consultancy (mandatory volume, competitively bid, firm substitutable even though the study is not) and us-secondary-market-shift (regulated utilities earning an allowed return on relocated load). ARCH-003 three times and INVERTED every time, which is itself the finding: organized-opposition and state-moratoria-and-siting-law are uninvestable order-book owners in the classic shape, and then hyperscale-buildout-demand, the link that on every prior chain would be the uninvestable anchor, is fully listed and the most crowded name set in the market. ARCH-004 once, translated from a material to a permit: water-permitting-and-hydrology scores on substitutability (closed-loop and direct-to-chip route the water away) times logistics (water cannot be hauled, so areas near Phoenix now limit all development). ARCH-005 once and declared, see the BLK-04 note. ARCH-006 twice and at a new scale: us-secondary-market-shift and offshore-and-periphery-capacity are the counter-response archetype at jurisdictional rather than geopolitical scale. ABSENCE CHECKS, recorded because a missing archetype is a finding and not a gap to pad. ARCH-001 does NOT fire: there is no manufacturing-capacity gate anywhere on this chain, the gates are legal and hydrological, and inventing a fabrication link to reach a familiar shape would have been padding. ARCH-007 does NOT fire in shape, no semiconductor layer sits on this chain at all, but its LESSON binds at hyperscale-buildout-demand and is applied there.

ARCH-006 note for the log, third instance in three chains and a third sign. On tibet-mega-dam the counter-response link WAS the money corner (opportunity). On russian-diesel-ban the second instance pointed the other way, the supply answer that ENDS the trade (risk). Here the third instance is an opportunity again but at a NEW SCALE: the reacting party is a US county or a European periphery, not a nation state, and the reaction is competitive rather than retaliatory. Three instances, three shapes. Not auto-applied to _archetypes.md, because widening a HARDENED archetype's definition from geopolitical to jurisdictional is outside the repair lane. ESCALATED for Ron.

FOUR STAGES CHECKED AND NOT BUILT, recorded rather than invented or silently duplicated. (a) Closed-loop and waterless COOLING HARDWARE. Real and directly caused by these rules (ITIF: Microsoft data centers consuming zero water for cooling by recirculating through a closed-loop direct-to-chip system), but its issuer set is ai-infrastructure/liquid-cooling's (VRT, MOD, NVT) and building it here would have been a second, less defensible duplication on top of the one BLK-04 already required. The fact is carried in water-permitting-and-hydrology.capture_inputs.shared_bom instead. Both sources for it were refused (Schneider Electric blog HTTP 403, DatacenterDynamics HTTP 403), which independently would have failed the citation bar. (b) BEHIND-THE-METER GENERATION as the permitting workaround. Cited and real (LandGate: behind-the-meter generation at more than 25 percent of new US data center capacity), but the generation hardware and its emissions permitting are the subject of rank-8 minor-nsr-permits (SIG-20260830-05), which is not on disk yet, so building it here would have created the exact triple-count BLK-04 names. Named in utility-ratemaking capture_inputs as the route around that link. (c) INTERCONNECTION QUEUE AND TRANSMISSION BUILDOUT. This is ai-infrastructure/grid-interconnect; its consequence is carried inside entitled-powered-land (six-year PJM waits, $4,000 per megawatt deposits) rather than given a third shared link. (d) TAX ABATEMENT AND INCENTIVE CLAWBACK. Real, and states are conditioning sales-tax exemptions, but nothing fetched this run put a dated number on the flow and there is no listed layer, so an honest 11-link map beats a padded 12.

SOURCES REFUSED, none of them cited: Schneider Electric datacenter blog (HTTP 403), DatacenterDynamics (HTTP 403), SEPA (HTTP 403), NBC News (HTTP 403), Environment+Energy Leader (HTTP 403), Data Centre Magazine (HTTP 403), Tom's Hardware (returned navigation shell only, no article body). Twenty-one URLs were opened successfully and seventeen of them are cited and every evidence item on this map carries a verbatim source_excerpt from one of them. LandGate's byline is relative (2 days ago as fetched on 2026-08-30) so its source_date is derived, not printed; that is the only derived date on the chain. Data Center Watch's Q1 2026 page returned no publication date, so it is not cited directly; its figures reach the map through Futura-Sciences (2026-08-28) and programs.com (2026-08-26), both dated and both fetched.

changelog.change: new chain from SIG-20260830-04 (US states converting data-center backlash into binding permitting freezes; impact 63.1, band REACHABLE, IMP-20260830-08). 11 links, 16 edges, upstream first with organized-opposition at position 1 and hyperscale-buildout-demand at position 11. Every link and every edge carries dated evidence with a verbatim source_excerpt from a page fetched this run; 21 distinct URLs opened and 17 cited, 7 refused (6 x HTTP 403, 1 returning no article body) and none of the refused pages was cited. power-equipment-shared at position 8 is a DECLARED duplicate of ai-infrastructure/power-equipment per campaign blocker BLK-04. heat is null on all 11 links and scenarios is empty by contract: run heat is next.

links.name: Organized local opposition
links.role: The raw input the rest of this map processes: organised residents, county boards and petition drives that turn a proposed campus into a contested one, which is what makes permission something a developer has to buy rather than apply for.

evidence.claim: The total number of active opposition groups reached 833 across 49 states by March 2026, and local opposition delayed or halted at least 75 U.S. data center projects during the first quarter of 2026, representing roughly $130 billion in combined capital investment.
evidence.source_name: Futura-Sciences, How a three-month uprising froze $130 billion of US data centers
source_excerpt: The total number of active opposition groups reached 833 across 49 states by March 2026
Local opposition delayed or halted at least 75 U.S. data center projects during the first quarter of 2026. These stalled facilities represent roughly $130 billion in combined capital investment.
Community opposition centers primarily on regional electrical grid strain and water consumption from cooling systems.

evidence.claim: 94 Total Local Moratoriums and Bans Have Passed in 2026, 40 States Have an Active Data Center Ban or Moratorium In Place, and Only 4 States Have No Statewide Data Center Restrictions Currently on Record.
evidence.source_name: Programs.com, Data Center Moratoriums by State: Tracker and Statistics (2026)
source_excerpt: 94 Total Local Moratoriums and Bans Have Passed in 2026
40 States Have an Active Data Center Ban or Moratorium In Place
Only 4 States Have No Statewide Data Center Restrictions Currently on Record
Alaska, Hawaii, West Virginia, and Wyoming are the only states where there are no data center moratoriums at a local or state level.

evidence.claim: CBAs are legally binding contracts between project developers and host municipalities and/or local community groups, under which the developer agrees to provide specified benefits to the community in which it wishes to operate, and, in return, the community agrees to not oppose or to support the project.
evidence.source_name: Columbia Climate Law Blog, Community Benefits Agreements and Data Center Development
source_excerpt: CBAs are legally binding contracts between project developers and host municipalities and/or local community groups, under which the developer agrees to provide specified benefits to the community in which it wishes to operate, and, in return, the community agrees to not oppose or to support the project.
Negotiating CBAs in the data center context is still an emerging practice so there are few direct examples from which to draw.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-003 inverted, first of two on this chain: this link sets every downstream link's schedule and there is no instrument for it. Not CHOKE_POINT because opposition on its own is routable, a developer can move counties; it becomes a choke point only when a state converts it into law at position 2.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: None, and that is the point: 833 groups across 49 states is a distributed veto, not a cartel, so there is no counterparty to buy out at this stage.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Nobody on this link. The money this link creates first appears two links down, at permitting consultancy and at community benefit, and is paid by the developer.
capture_inputs.substitutability: The developer's substitute for consent is relocation, which is why us-secondary-market-shift and offshore-and-periphery-capacity exist on this map at all.

links.name: State moratoria and siting law
links.role: The stage where backlash becomes a binding constraint: an executive order or statute that holds discretionary permits in abeyance, plus the state environmental review that has to finish before anybody can build again.

evidence.claim: New York Executive Order No 62 applies to data centers that consume or can consume 50 megawatts of energy or more and directs the Department of Environmental Conservation to hold in abeyance all applications for any discretionary permit, approval, license, or similar form of permission for the construction or expansion of a data center.
evidence.source_name: Governor Kathy Hochul, Executive Order No. 62 (official executive order text)
source_excerpt: No 62: Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers in New York While the State Develops Higher Standards for Data Center Development and Benefits Blueprint to Support Localities
consume or can consume 50 megawatts of energy or more
hold in abeyance all applications for any discretionary permit, approval, license, or similar form of permission for the construction or expansion of a data center

evidence.claim: DPS must hold a technical conference by December 31, 2026, and publish a white paper discussing a comprehensive proposal for addressing issues associated with large-load connections by February 12, 2027.
evidence.source_name: Davis Wright Tremaine, Key Takeaways from New York Data Center Permitting Pause Under Executive Order No. 62
source_excerpt: DPS must hold a technical conference by December 31, 2026, and publish a white paper discussing a comprehensive proposal for addressing issues associated with large-load connections by February 12, 2027.
The Executive Order sets no deadline for DPS to complete the GEIS.

evidence.claim: The Generic Environmental Impact Statement the freeze waits on must assess energy demand, water use and quality, air quality, disproportionate impacts on disadvantaged communities, and noise levels.
evidence.source_name: Governor Kathy Hochul, Executive Order No. 62 (official executive order text)
source_excerpt: energy demand, water use and quality, air quality, disproportionate impacts on disadvantaged communities, and noise levels
hold in abeyance all applications for any discretionary permit, approval, license, or similar form of permission for the construction or expansion of a data center

evidence.claim: Minnesota became the first state to establish a formal water-permitting requirement for large data centers, and California and Arizona require power plant developers to evaluate water-efficiency options including recirculating and dry cooling as part of the siting process.
evidence.source_name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, The Data Center Water Problem Is Soluble
source_excerpt: Minnesota became the first state to establish a formal water-permitting requirement for large data centers.
California and Arizona require power plant developers to evaluate water-efficiency options—including recirculating and dry cooling—as part of the siting process.

evidence.claim: As of June 2026, 14 US states have considered or are actively considering some form of moratorium or restrictions on data center development, and states and counties that have not yet triggered political friction around data centers retain the advantage.
evidence.source_name: Build Inc, Data Center Moratoriums in 2026: What the Policy Shift Means for Developers
source_excerpt: As of June 2026, 14 US states have considered or are actively considering some form of moratorium or restrictions on data center development.

States and counties that have not yet triggered political friction around data centers retain the advantage. Secondary markets in the US Southeast, parts of the Midwest, and select Texas markets benefit precisely because they have not accumulated the community opposition that characterizes Northern Virginia or metropolitan New York.

evidence.claim: AI-scale power and land needs are pushing operators onto secondary sites, hyper scale sites average 175 km from a hub city, up from 46 km, and greenfield rises from 8% to 39% of the 2026 to 2028 pipeline.
evidence.source_name: JLL, EMEA Data Centre Mid-Year 2026 Report
source_excerpt: AI-scale power and land needs are pushing operators onto secondary sites; those with power there capture the growth.
hyper scale sites within it average 175 km from a hub city, up from 46 km.
Greenfield rises from 8% to 39% of the 2026 to 2028 pipeline.
Availability of contiguous, high-density space is scarce across every FLAP-D market.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-003 inverted, second instance: a hold with no fixed end date, tied to a study with no deadline, gates every discretionary permit above a 50 MW threshold in the state. There is nothing to buy at this stage, which is exactly why the ticker list is empty rather than thin.

capture_inputs.substitutability: Zero inside the jurisdiction and total outside it. That asymmetry, not the freeze itself, is what the rest of this map prices.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: The binding constraint is the study calendar, not construction: DEC holds applications until DPS files the final GEIS, and the order sets no deadline for that filing.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Nobody. This link is a cost imposed on the anchor and a revenue event for permitting consultancy, water consultancy and community benefit.

links.name: Utility ratemaking and large-load tariffs
links.role: The proceeding that decides who pays for the grid a data center needs: a special rate class, a minimum-take contract and an up-front capital contribution, all set at a state commission rather than negotiated with the developer.

evidence.claim: As of May 2026, twenty-three states have approved at least one large load tariff, and another seven states have pending large load tariffs; the tariff requires data centers in that class to pay at least 85% of their contracted capacity or billing demand even if they use less and enter into initial contracts for a minimum of twelve years.
evidence.source_name: Columbia Climate Law Blog, Data Center Regulation: What Local Governments Should Know about Large-Load Tariffs and Clean Transition Tariffs
source_excerpt: as of May 2026, twenty-three states have approved at least one large load tariff, and another seven states have pending large load tariffs.

The tariff requires data centers in that class to pay at least 85% of their contracted capacity or billing demand (even if they use less) and enter into initial contracts for a minimum of twelve years.
Ohio's PUC approved a proposed tariff filed by the utility AEP Ohio
In Virginia, the state with the largest concentration of data centers, the State Corporation Commission approved a new large-load tariff in 2025

evidence.claim: Large load tariffs determine how much data centers must pay and the conditions for how they connect to the grid, requiring new data centers to bear the incremental costs from capital expenditures needed to serve them.
evidence.source_name: Columbia Climate Law Blog, Data Center Regulation: What Local Governments Should Know about Large-Load Tariffs and Clean Transition Tariffs
source_excerpt: determine how much they [must] pay and the conditions for how they connect to the grid
requiring new data centers to bear the incremental costs from capital expenditures needed to serve them
Other states have enacted, or are considering, legislation that directs PUCs to regulate large loads, including Oregon, Texas, and Virginia.

evidence.claim: More than 300 data center-related bills have been introduced in 30 states' legislatures in the first six weeks of 2026, TX S.B. 6 requires developers to pay for interconnection studies and infrastructure upgrades, and Oregon requires large energy use facilities using 20 MW or more to ensure that grid infrastructure costs driven by such facilities are allocated to their developers.
evidence.source_name: ArentFox Schiff, State Regulation of Data Centers in 2026 - A Shifting Landscape
source_excerpt: More than 300 data center-related bills have been introduced in 30 states' legislatures in the first six weeks of 2026
TX S.B. 6 requires developers to pay for interconnection studies and infrastructure upgrades
Large energy use facilities (using 20 MW or more), such as data centers, to ensure that grid infrastructure costs driven by such facilities are allocated to their developers
At least 18 states have introduced bills creating special rate classes or infrastructure cost-sharing mandates for large energy users

bottleneck.note: A twelve-year minimum-take contract at 85% of contracted demand is the single hardest number on this map: it converts a siting fight into a balance-sheet obligation and it is set by a commission, not by either counterparty.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Total within a service territory and irrelevant across them: a large-load tariff is a monopoly's terms in one state, which is why the ticker list is a list of regulated utilities and not a competitive set.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Two different parties and they must not be conflated. The regulated utility earns an allowed return on the upgrade (ARCH-002 economics, capped by construction). The rate-case and load-forecast consultants (CRAI, ICFI, plus private Guidehouse and Concentric) bill fees with no rate base at all.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Behind-the-meter generation is the developer's route around this link entirely, which is why it is named as a dropped stage in the chain notes rather than pretended away.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: The capital contribution this link extracts is spent at power-equipment-shared, which is ai-infrastructure/power-equipment. See that link's declaration.

links.name: Permitting and environmental consultancy
links.role: The firms that produce the environmental impact statement, the hydrology and noise and air modelling and the permit application itself; a freeze converts a filing exercise into a multi-year study programme somebody bills for.

evidence.claim: New data center facilities are increasingly running into the same constraint set of water availability, environmental permitting, local infrastructure capacity, and community resistance, and Tetra Tech positions its high-end consulting services for water supplies and environmental impact mitigation as increasingly critical to gaining community support for data center projects.
evidence.source_name: Yahoo Finance, Why Tetra Tech (TTEK) Is Becoming More Relevant as Data Centers Face Water and Permitting Constraints
source_excerpt: new facilities are increasingly running into the same constraint set: water availability, environmental permitting, local infrastructure capacity, and community resistance.
high-end consulting services for water supplies and environmental impact mitigation are becoming increasingly critical to gaining community support for data center projects

evidence.claim: The four biggest firms by environmental and sustainability consulting revenue in the US, Tetra Tech, AECOM, WSP and Jacobs, made up over 40% of the total US E&S consulting market in 2024, and more than $25bn of E&S consulting revenue was generated in the US in 2024, with steady growth forecast out to 2029.
evidence.source_name: Environment Analyst Global, Tetra Tech, AECOM, WSP and Jacobs still dominate US E&S consulting
source_excerpt: The four biggest firms by environmental and sustainability (E&S) consulting revenue in the US – Tetra Tech, AECOM, WSP and Jacobs – made up over 40% of the total US E&S consulting market in 2024.
More than $25bn of E&S consulting revenue was generated in the US in 2024, with steady growth forecast out to 2029.
Water-related services made up over half of the consultancy's E&S consulting revenue in the US in 2024

evidence.claim: Companies should promptly review their permitting status and development timelines, examining whether all required state permits have been issued, whether applications are complete, and whether remaining approvals are discretionary or ministerial.
evidence.source_name: Davis Wright Tremaine, Key Takeaways from New York Data Center Permitting Pause Under Executive Order No. 62
source_excerpt: promptly review their permitting status and development timelines
whether all required state permits have been issued, whether applications are complete, whether remaining approvals are discretionary or ministerial
The Executive Order sets no deadline for DPS to complete the GEIS.

bottleneck.note: The work cannot be routed around, because the state named the studies it wants before it will lift the hold. It can be routed to a different firm, which is what caps the capture at this link.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Four firms hold over 40% of a US market above $25bn, which is concentration at the top and a long private tail below it (ERM, Ramboll, GHD, SLR, Golder).
capture_inputs.substitutability: The STUDY is not substitutable, the FIRM is. That is ARCH-002 wearing a consultancy costume: mandatory volume, competitively bid, so record the capture ceiling before the heat run assumes scarcity pricing.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Nothing fetched this run isolates a data-center permitting margin at any of these firms. Every figure on this link is a whole-company or whole-market number, so the capture score must not be read off the market size.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: The qualification is relationship and precedent, not equipment: the firm that wrote a state's first GEIS is the natural bidder for the next one.

links.name: Water permitting and hydrology
links.role: The second permit nobody used to model: withdrawal rights, hydrological studies and community water impact assessments, which now sit on the critical path beside the interconnection queue.

evidence.claim: Water permitting timelines now rival electrical interconnection queues, water permitting timelines and local hydrological studies and community water impact assessments are now on the critical path alongside grid interconnection and planning consent, and projects totalling an estimated $156 billion were delayed or cancelled in 2025 alone.
evidence.source_name: Capacity, The hidden constraint that's stalling data centre build-out
source_excerpt: water permitting timelines now rival electrical interconnection queues
water permitting timelines, local hydrological studies and community water impact assessments are now on the critical path alongside grid interconnection and planning consent
Projects totalling an estimated $156 billion were delayed or cancelled in 2025 alone
More than 300 data centre-related bills were introduced in 30 US states in the first six weeks of 2026 alone

evidence.claim: Data centers directly consumed 17.4 billion gallons annually in 2023, and water consumed for electricity production requires a further 211 billion gallons, 12x the amount of direct consumption.
evidence.source_name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, The Data Center Water Problem Is Soluble
source_excerpt: Data centers directly consumed 17.4 billion gallons annually in 2023, and water consumed for electricity production requires a further 211 billion gallons—12x the amount of direct consumption.
Water is a convenient hook on which to hang more general opposition to data centers (and AI).
All told, that would amount to less than 1 percent of total U.S. water consumption.

evidence.claim: Some areas near Phoenix now limit all development because there is no more potable water available, and Microsoft has introduced new AI-optimized data centers that will consume zero water for cooling operations by continuously recirculating fluid through a closed-loop direct-to-chip system.
evidence.source_name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, The Data Center Water Problem Is Soluble
source_excerpt: Some areas near Phoenix, for example, now limit all development because there is no more potable water available.
Microsoft has introduced new AI-optimized data centers that will consume zero water for cooling operations by continuously recirculating fluid through a closed-loop direct-to-chip system.
Some—including Google, AWS, and Microsoft—are also using municipal wastewater to avoid relying on scarce potable water.

bottleneck.note: ARCH-004 translated from a material to a permit. Criticality is substitutability times logistics and both legs are cited: closed-loop and direct-to-chip designs substitute the water away, and water cannot be hauled to a site, so the constraint is local and absolute where it binds (areas near Phoenix now limit all development).

capture_inputs.substitutability: High at the design stage and zero after it. A campus designed closed-loop routes around this link entirely; a campus already permitted on evaporative cooling cannot.
capture_inputs.logistics_or_qualification: Water is the one input on this map with no logistics option: 17.4 billion gallons of direct consumption is a local claim on a local aquifer, and ITIF records areas near Phoenix that now limit all development for that reason.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established by anything fetched this run. ITIF's own framing is that the total is less than 1 percent of US water consumption, which argues the scarcity is political and local rather than national, and a national water-scarcity trade is not what this link supports.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: The closed-loop and direct-to-chip HARDWARE this rule creates demand for is ai-infrastructure/liquid-cooling (VRT, MOD, NVT). It is deliberately not a link here. See the chain notes.

links.name: Community benefit and consent
links.role: The negotiated price of permission: community benefit agreements, host fees and community investment funds, plus the land-use counsel and public-affairs shops that write them, which is the one place on this map where consent is literally bought.

evidence.claim: Lancaster, Pennsylvania's data center community benefits agreement includes $20.25 million in total contributions, comprising $10 million to Lancaster County Community Foundation, a $250,000 additional contribution, and $10 million to the City's Sustainable Development and Clean Energy Fund.
evidence.source_name: Columbia Climate Law Blog, Community Benefits Agreements and Data Center Development
source_excerpt: $20.25 million
$10 million to Lancaster County Community Foundation
$250,000 additional contribution
$10 million to the City's Sustainable Development and Clean Energy Fund
Negotiating CBAs in the data center context is still an emerging practice so there are few direct examples from which to draw.

evidence.claim: Speed to power is the primary criteria driving site selection, followed by community support, latency and proximity to customers.
evidence.source_name: JLL, 2026 Global Data Center Outlook
source_excerpt: Speed to power is the primary criteria driving site selection, followed by community support, latency and proximity to customers.
Energy infrastructure has emerged as the critical bottleneck constraining expansion.

bottleneck.note: Real and growing but not yet a gate: the largest data-center CBA anyone has cited is $20.25 million against campuses costing billions, and Columbia's own note is that the practice is still emerging with few direct examples. Priced as an entry ticket, not as a toll.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: None visible. The negotiating layer is local land-use law firms and regional public-affairs shops, essentially all private; FCN and WPP.L are listed seeds for a universe search, not evidence that either does this work.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: The host community, not a supplier. $20.25 million went to a county foundation and a city fund, which is a transfer to the jurisdiction rather than revenue to an issuer, and that is the honest reason this link is MOSTLY_PRIVATE.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Substitutable by relocation, like every consent cost on this map, and only by relocation.

links.name: Entitled and powered land
links.role: The asset a freeze manufactures: a site that already holds its entitlements, its water permit and its interconnection position, worth more the longer permission takes to obtain anywhere else.

evidence.claim: Interconnection queue waits exceed six years in parts of PJM, non-refundable readiness deposits reach $4,000 per megawatt and roughly $1 million for a 250 MW project, and power availability measured in real terms like available transfer capacity and substation offtake headroom now has to be confirmed before any other factor.
evidence.source_name: LandGate, Why Power, Not Land, Is the Real Bottleneck in Data Center Site Selection
source_excerpt: interconnection queue waits exceeding six years in parts of PJM
non-refundable readiness deposits reaching $4,000 per megawatt
roughly $1 million for a 250 MW project
power availability, measured in real terms like available transfer capacity and substation offtake headroom, now has to be confirmed before any other factor
grid capacity was, in most markets, simply available. That assumption no longer holds

evidence.claim: A one-year moratorium in a market where you hold an option means your feasibility clock is running, your interconnection queue position is aging, and your capital is tied up, and regulatory risk now precedes power risk in some markets.
evidence.source_name: Build Inc, Data Center Moratoriums in 2026: What the Policy Shift Means for Developers
source_excerpt: A one-year moratorium in a market where you hold an option means your feasibility clock is running, your interconnection queue position is aging, and your capital is tied up.
Regulatory risk now precedes power risk in some markets. A site with strong grid access but in a jurisdiction trending toward moratorium is not a clean opportunity.
For institutional developers, these restrictions are not just political noise. They are site selection constraints that belong in the first pass of diligence, not the confirmatory phase.
